title: 梅花
author: Wang Anshi

translation: a few branches of plum stand by the corner wall
they open all alone in the bitter cold
from far off i know they are not snow
because a hidden fragrance drifts to me

appreciation: A plum tree blooms by a wall in deep winter, and the poet knows from its scent that the white on the branches is flower, not snow. The poem turns a small observation into a quiet statement about character: beauty that survives the cold needs no audience. Its last line is one of the most quoted images of inner worth in Chinese poetry.
